question.text: Ashoka Cat II AIF has a small investment team and outsources its back-office. The Manager appoints an 'Operating Manager' (sometimes called a Chief Operating Officer or Head of Fund Operations) who coordinates between the custodian, RTA, fund administrator, auditor and valuer. Which statement BEST describes the Operating Manager's role from the ecosystem-governance standpoint?

answer.text: Single-point coordinator across service providers — escalation owner for breaks, reconciliations, NAV sign-offs, PPM-audit liaison and LPAC operational updates — NOT a SEBI-registered role but critical for integrated ecosystem governance.
SEBI-registered intermediary with a separate fit-and-proper test distinct from the Manager entity.
Equivalent to the Trustee and can override IC decisions.
Replaces the Compliance Officer and Chief Investment Officer when appointed.

explanation.text: The Logic: An Operating Manager/COO/Head of Fund Operations typically serves as the single-point coordinator across custodian, RTA, fund administrator, auditor and valuer — owning reconciliation breaks, NAV sign-off workflow, PPM-audit liaison and LPAC operational updates. It is an internal Manager-entity role, not a separately SEBI-registered intermediary, and it does not displace or override the Trustee, CIO, or Compliance Officer. The Trap: Option B invents a separate SEBI registration that does not exist. Option C wrongly equates the role with the Trustee's fiduciary powers. Option D incorrectly claims it absorbs CIO/CO responsibilities, which are distinct registered positions. Note: The Operating Manager/COO/Head of Fund Operations role as a single-point ecosystem coordinator is not specifically defined in the cited workbook chapter (FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 114-116, 357-358, 552), which covers other service-provider roles instead. The framing above is general industry/operational practice for AIF managers.
